methodologyNotes: Covers 12 gravel bikes a buyer actively cross-shops in 2026, spanning race-focused carbon (Crux, Grail CF SLX, Aspero-5, Racemax² Italia), all-road/endurance (Checkpoint SL, Topstone Carbon, Revolt Advanced), and extreme-clearance/adventure builds (OPEN WI.DE., BMC URS 01, ENVE MOG). priceUsd is the US MSRP of the lowest-priced complete-bike configuration of the named model that could be verified in USD; where a model is sold in multiple build kits, priceNote states which build the price and specs refer to. priceUsd is null when no USD price could be independently verified (e.g. a brand only publishes GBP/CAD pricing, or its US storefront returned repeated bot-protection errors to automated access during research). Several manufacturer storefronts (Specialized, Salsa, Santa Cruz, BMC, ENVE, 3T — mostly Shopify-hosted) returned HTTP 403/429 to repeated automated fetches during this research pass; for those, the manufacturer's own page content was used where it loaded successfully, and reputable independent sources (road.cc, GearJunkie, BikeRadar, Escape Collective, bikepacking.com) or established US bicycle retailers were used as primary/corroborating sources instead, with the access limitation noted per-product in provenance. weight_lb is the manufacturer-claimed or reviewer-measured COMPLETE BIKE weight for the specific build cited — never a frame-only weight — and is left null when only a frame weight was published. accessory_mounts_count is populated ONLY when a source explicitly stated a countable number of mount points (e.g. "three bottle mounts"); qualitative mount descriptions ("multiple gear/bottle mounts", "fork and top tube mounts") were NOT converted into an invented count and are left null — a null beats a guess. drivetrain_speeds is the rear-cassette speed count (e.g. 12 for a 1x12 or 2x12 drivetrain). gearing_range is written "chainring(s)t x cassette-loT-hiT". 3T's original "Exploro RaceMax" was discontinued and succeeded in 3T's current lineup by the "Racemax² Italia" (700c, higher clearance) and "Racemax WPNT" (650b-capable) — the Racemax² Italia is used here as the closest current equivalent, and this substitution is called out in its provenance. All prices and specs were checked against the cited source(s) on accessedAt; no spec, price, or image was invented — unverifiable fields are null.

products.name: Canyon Grail CF SLX 8 AXS
products.priceNote: US MSRP $6,099 per Canyon's official product page, which showed the bike at a temporary 20%-off price of $4,899 at time of access.
products.provenance: Fetched Canyon's official Grail CF SLX 8 AXS product page (model 4475), which confirms the SRAM Force AXS XPLR 1x13 drivetrain (40t chainring, 10-46t cassette), CF SLX carbon frame, 42mm tire clearance, 12x100/12x142 thru-axles, a manufacturer-claimed 18.08lb (size M) weight, and integrated LOAD downtube storage plus Gear Groove cockpit mounting (no single enumerated mount count was given, so accessory_mounts_count is null). Cyclingnews' independent 2025 review of the same AXS build corroborates the weight (~18lb), tire clearance, and drivetrain. The image file was downloaded directly from Canyon's own DMA asset CDN (URL taken from the live product page, .jpg suffix appended to force a static format) and visually confirmed to show this exact bike.

products.name: Specialized Crux Comp - Shimano GRX
products.priceNote: US retail price observed at $3,199.99-$3,999.99 across colorways/retailers (BicycleWarehouse, Dunbar Cycles both list the 2026 Crux Comp - Shimano GRX); specialized.com itself blocked repeated automated access (403) so its own listed USD price could not be re-confirmed directly. A Canadian retailer (CycleNeron) separately lists the same bike at C$4,999.99 regular MSRP, consistent with this USD range.
products.provenance: specialized.com returned HTTP 403 to every direct automated fetch attempt in this research pass, so the BikeExchange mirror of the 2026 Crux Comp listing (which republishes Specialized's own commercetools-hosted product data and imagery) was used to confirm identity: FACT 10r carbon frame, Rider-First Engineered geometry, flat-mount disc, UDH dropout, threaded BB, Shimano GRX 1x12 with 40t/10-45t gearing, 700x38mm Pathfinder Pro tires with 47mm/650bx2.1in clearance, and a claimed 8.55kg (18lb 13.6oz) weight. A US price could not be independently re-verified via direct fetch given the manufacturer block; the $3,199.99-$3,999.99 range and CAD MSRP are the best available US-market signal. The hero product image is Specialized's own commerce-CDN photo (pulled from the BikeExchange listing's markup) and was downloaded and visually confirmed to show this Crux Comp in a purple/pink colorway with a GRX crank and "CRUX" fork branding.

products.name: Trek Checkpoint SL 7 AXS Gen 3
products.priceNote: $5,700 as stated in GearJunkie's tested review; trekbikes.com is a JavaScript-rendered storefront that did not expose its price or full spec table to automated fetching in this research pass, so this reviewer-reported figure is the best available verification.
products.provenance: trekbikes.com's live page confirms this exact model exists at this URL (Checkpoint SL 7 AXS Gen 3) but its React-rendered content did not expose price, weight, or full specs to automated fetching. GearJunkie's December 2024 tested review supplies the verified detail instead: 500 Series OCLV carbon frame, SRAM Force AXS 12-speed (40t / 10-44t), 50mm tire clearance, 700c wheels, a reviewer-measured 19lb 9oz (size L), and a $5,700 price at time of review. Axle spacing was not stated by either source, so it is left null rather than assumed. No manufacturer or reputable-outlet image could be sourced within this pass without misattributing an editorial photographer's copyrighted photo as Trek's own, so the image field is omitted.

products.name: Cervelo Cervélo Áspero-5 GRX Di2
products.priceNote: $8,850 is the lowest-priced complete-bike build shown on Cervelo's official build table (GRX RX827 Di2); Force AXS 1 is $9,000 and Red AXS 1 is $12,650. A frameset-only option is $5,500.
products.provenance: Cervelo's official Aspero-5 page lists a full builds table: Red AXS 1 ($12,650, 48/10-52t), GRX RX827 Di2 1 ($8,850, 48/10-51t), Force AXS 1 ($9,000, 48/10-52t), and a $5,500 frameset, all sharing a carbon frame, 45mm max tire clearance, 700c Reserve wheels, threaded ceramic BB, and downtube internal storage. The cheapest complete build (GRX Di2) is used here. Escape Collective's long-term review of the identical GRX Di2 build corroborates the model and drivetrain. Complete-bike weight and axle spacing were not stated on the fetched page (only a 920g frame weight is published elsewhere, which is not used here since it is not a complete-bike figure), so both are left null. The image URL was extracted directly from the live cervelo.com page markup (images.prismic.io/cervelo/... is Cervelo's own CMS asset namespace); the file exceeded this pipeline's inline preview size limit so it was not re-rendered for visual confirmation, but its source domain and page origin are unambiguous.

products.name: 3T Racemax² Italia
products.priceNote: No verified USD price found: 3T's US storefront (us.3t.bike) returned HTTP 429 to every automated fetch attempt in this pass. UK pricing is confirmed via road.cc: frameset from £5,310; complete builds from £8,763 (Shimano GRX Di2 2x) up to £11,595 (Campagnolo Super Record 2x13).
products.provenance: 3T discontinued the "Exploro RaceMax" name; its current successor in 3T's lineup is the "Racemax² Italia" (700c-only, up to 51mm clearance in 1x) alongside the separate 650b-capable "Racemax WPNT". road.cc's review (the manufacturer's own US and global storefronts were unreachable via automated fetch, returning 429s repeatedly) confirms the Jazz Carbon frame, 700c wheels, 51mm tire clearance (1x)/48mm (2x), 12x100/12x142 thru-axles, a reviewer-measured 8,960g (19.75lb) test-bike weight, and pricing only in GBP across four groupset options (Shimano GRX Di2 2x12, SRAM Force XPLR, SRAM RED XPLR, Campagnolo Super Record 2x13) — since no single build is the confirmed "base" and no USD figure exists, groupset/drivetrain_speeds/gearing_range/priceUsd are left null rather than guessed. Bikerumor's first-ride coverage corroborates the model, frame material, and tire clearance figures. No manufacturer press image could be sourced; the only located photos were credited to road.cc's own photographer, so the image field is omitted rather than mislabeled as a 3T press photo.

products.name: Giant Revolt Advanced 1
products.priceNote: US MSRP $3,200 per Giant's official 2026 (MY26) product page.
products.provenance: Giant's official MY26 Revolt Advanced 1 page confirms: Advanced-grade composite frame with a two-position flip-chip dropout (45mm short / 53mm long tire clearance), SRAM Apex 1 12-speed (40t chainring, SRAM PG-1231 11-44t cassette), 12mm front / 12x142mm rear thru-axles, in-frame storage bag, and a $3,200 US MSRP. Velo's 2026 launch coverage corroborates the redesigned Advanced frame and flip-chip clearance changes. Giant does not publish a complete-bike weight on this page ("have your local dealer weigh it"), so weight_lb is null; wheel size is not spelled out verbatim on the page but is unambiguous from the 700c-convention tire-clearance figures and the model's history. The hero image URL was extracted directly from the live product page and downloaded/visually confirmed to show this exact bike (grey/blue Revolt Advanced with drop bars and a GRX-style crank).

products.name: Salsa Warbird C GRX 610 1x
products.priceNote: US MSRP $3,199, consistent across multiple authorized Salsa dealers (Freewheel Bike, Cedar Bicycle, Alex's Bicycle Pro Shop) at time of access; Freewheel showed a $2,599.99 sale price.
products.provenance: Salsa's official product description (mirrored identically on authorized-dealer pages after salsacycles.com itself began returning 429s mid-session) confirms a high-modulus carbon frame accepting 700x45mm or 650bx51mm tires, Shimano GRX 610 1x12 (40t/10-45t), 12x100/12x142 thru-axles, and an explicit mount count: "2-3 bottle mounts inside the main triangle (56cm+ frames get 3), 1 accessory mount on the underside of the down tube, and 2 bottle mounts possible on the fork" — summed here as 6 for the largest frame sizes (the only accessory_mounts_count in this dataset derived from the source's own explicit numbers rather than a qualitative description). Price ($3,199 MSRP) is corroborated identically across three independent Salsa dealers. Complete-bike weight is not published. The image is Salsa's own dealer-syndicated product photo (sefiles.net is the shared image library Salsa provides to its authorized retailers) and was downloaded and visually confirmed to show this exact bike (grey/black Warbird with "SALSA" down-tube branding and a GRX drivetrain).

products.name: Santa Cruz Stigmata Apex
products.priceNote: US MSRP $4,149 for the base-level SRAM Apex build, the least expensive of five 2026 Stigmata Carbon CC complete builds ($4,149-$7,549); a $2,799 frameset is also offered.
products.provenance: bikepacking.com's launch article on the 2026 Santa Cruz Stigmata (santacruzbicycles.com itself returned repeated 429s to automated fetches during this pass) confirms: Carbon CC frame/fork, UDH dropout, 700x50mm tire clearance, threaded 68mm BB, 27.2mm seatpost, internal frame storage, and "three bottle mounts" (used directly as accessory_mounts_count=3, the only explicit number given). Five complete builds range $4,149 (base SRAM Apex) to $7,549, plus a $2,799 frameset; the base Apex build is used here for pricing. Groupset speed count is assumed 12 for SRAM Apex 1x but the exact chainring/cassette combination for this specific build, complete-bike weight, and axle spacing were not stated in the accessible source, so gearing_range, weight_lb, and axle_type are left null. No manufacturer image could be retrieved (santacruzbicycles.com blocked repeated fetch attempts), so the image field is omitted rather than substituting an unverified photo.

products.name: OPEN WI.DE. 2.0
products.priceNote: $8,000 is OPEN's advertised price for its SRAM Force AXS XPLR / Zipp XPLR complete-bike build, the lower of two factory complete builds (Red AXS / Zipp XPLR is $10,200). OPEN more commonly sells the WI.DE as a bare frameset for a dealer build ($3,200 raw / $4,000 painted for the 2.0 generation), and opencycle.com's own product page did not display pricing at time of access.
products.provenance: OPEN's official WI.DE 2.0 page confirms a TRCinTRS carbon frame accepting 650bx2.4in (61mm) or 700cx46mm tires, Carbon-Ti X-12 100x12mm front / 142x12mm rear thru-axles, and compatibility with 1x SRAM XPLR, Shimano GRX, or Campagnolo Ekar (chainring range 38-46t, no single gearing range confirmed for a specific build so left null); it did not display complete-bike pricing. Cycling Weekly's coverage of the same 2.0 launch corroborates the model and headlines an even larger 66mm clearance claim, a minor discrepancy against OPEN's own stated 61mm 650b figure (the manufacturer's own figure is used here). The $8,000/$10,200 complete-bike prices reflect OPEN's factory build-kit pricing found via retailer/press coverage rather than opencycle.com's own storefront. Frame-only weight (~1040g) is published but not used for weight_lb since it is not a complete-bike figure. No usable image was found — opencycle.com's product images are lazy-loaded via JavaScript and only base64 placeholders were retrievable — so the image field is omitted.

products.name: Cannondale Topstone Carbon 3 GRX - 1x
products.priceNote: US MSRP $3,799, shown on cannondale.com at a sale price of $3,099 at time of access.

specs.frame_material: Topstone Carbon with Kingpin suspension, Proportional Response construction

products.provenance: Cannondale's official MY25 Topstone Carbon 3 GRX-1x page confirms the Kingpin-suspension carbon frame, 700c wheels, 12x100/12x142 thru-axles, Shimano GRX 610/820 blended 1x12 drivetrain (40t chainring, 10-51t cassette), and tire clearance up to 52mm single-ring; it did not display a price directly (region-gated pricing). Stowe Sports' retailer listing of the identical SKU corroborates identity and shows $3,099 as a sale price against a $3,799 regular price, which is used here as MSRP. Complete-bike weight is not published on the fetched page. The hero image was pulled directly from Cannondale's Widen digital-asset-management CDN (linked from the live product page) and downloaded/visually confirmed to show this exact bike (teal/black Topstone Carbon with "Cannondale" down-tube branding and a GRX crank).

products.name: BMC URS 01 TWO
products.priceNote: US MSRP $5,999, shown on BMC's official US site at a current price of $4,499. This is the lowest-priced URS 01 build independently identified by name and price in this research pass; other sources suggest URS 01 pricing spans roughly $3,199-$8,399 across additional build tiers not individually confirmed here.
products.provenance: BMC's official US URS 01 collection page lists "URS 01 TWO" at $4,499 (regular price $5,999) and "URS 01 ONE" at $5,999 (regular $8,399); us.bmc-switzerland.com began returning HTTP 429 to further automated requests partway through this research pass, so the exact groupset fitted to the TWO build could not be independently confirmed and is left null rather than guessed. BMC's URS 01 platform page (fetched successfully) corroborates the shared platform spec: carbon frame, 47mm tire clearance, and fork/top-tube/downtube accessory mounts plus downtube storage (described only qualitatively, not as a numbered count, so accessory_mounts_count is null). Wheel size (700c) reflects the URS 01 platform's standard spec. Complete-bike weight, axle spacing, and gearing range for the TWO build specifically were not available from accessible sources and are left null. No manufacturer image of the TWO build could be retrieved within this pass (product-page and retailer-mirror fetches were rate-limited), so the image field is omitted.

products.name: ENVE MOG (GRX Di2 build)
products.priceNote: $8,799.99 is ENVE's starting price for the MOG Shimano GRX Di2 RX825 2x complete bike, the lowest-priced of ENVE's factory complete builds (SRAM builds start at $9,099.99). A frameset/chassis-only option is $5,500.
products.provenance: enve.com returned HTTP 429 to every automated fetch attempt in this pass, so BikeRadar's review of the GRX Di2 build was used as the primary spec source: ENVE M.O.D carbon frame/fork, T47 threaded BB, 12x142mm rear / 12x100mm front thru-axles, 700x50mm tire clearance, Shimano GRX Di2 1x11 (42t chainring, 11-42t cassette), integrated Cargo Bay downtube storage, and a tested complete-bike weight of 8.87kg (19.56lb). ENVE's own complete-bike product listing (surfaced via web search of its own site content, since direct fetch was blocked) independently confirms a $8,799.99 starting price for the GRX Di2 2x complete build — note this is a 2x reference from ENVE's current lineup while the reviewed test bike was a 1x11 build, so the drivetrain/gearing spec fields describe the reviewed bike, not necessarily the exact $8,799.99 SKU; this discrepancy is flagged rather than papered over. No accessory mount count was explicitly enumerated by either source. The only located product photo was credited to a BikeRadar staff photographer rather than ENVE, so the image field is omitted rather than mislabeled as an ENVE press photo.
